_comment: Template study config. Copy this file, rename it, and fill in your own corpus — pass it via --config. Required sections: languages, corpora, study, embedding_model, chunking, output. Everything after '_optional_sections_comment' is only read by specific scripts; delete sections for scripts you won't run. Language codes are your own choice (see README's Config section, 'Language codes') — this template uses 'en'/'fr' as illustrative placeholders only, not a requirement. Any key starting with '_' is treated as a comment and skipped everywhere the toolkit iterates a section, so you can annotate your own config the same way.

output._comment: Written under the working directory unless you set 'root' (or pass --output-root). Absolute paths are used as-is.

en._comment: spacy_model (+ optional spacy_model_fallback) is needed if this language is used with adjective_window.py or dependency_parsing.py, or as primary_language for cross_corpus_dependency.py. stanza_model is needed if this is your comparison_language. stopwords_file, keep_short_tokens, and adjective_suffixes are all optional tokenizer tuning — see README. stopwords_file is looked for next to this config file, under the working directory, then among the lists bundled with the package.

fr._comment: For cross_corpus_frequency.py, configure a stopwords_file for BOTH languages or for neither — removing stopwords from only one side biases the per-10k rates and Dunning scores.

author_a_work._comment: type is 'single_file' (one continuous text) or 'collection' (a directory of dated/grouped items, see author_a_collection below). path is relative to corpus_root / --corpus-root.
author_a_work.label: Author A's Work
author_a_work.author: author_a

author_a_collection._comment: For type 'collection': path is a directory containing one subdirectory per entry in 'groups', each holding .txt files (one file per dated/grouped item).
author_a_collection.label: Author A's Collection
author_a_collection.author: author_a

author_b_work._comment: strip_after_marker is optional: drop everything from a marker line onward, e.g. an editorial apparatus section.
author_b_work.label: Author B's Work
author_b_work.author: author_b

_optional_sections_comment: Everything below is optional. Each section is read by exactly one script — delete a section if you won't run that script.

lexical_richness._comment: Used by lexical_richness.py. mattr_window is in tokens; lower it for short texts, or the whole work collapses to a single TTR value. smoothing_window is in MATTR values.

term_frequency_clusters._comment: Used by term_frequency.py. One entry per concept cluster; 'terms' are surface forms in primary_language to count together.

adjective_window._comment: Used by adjective_window.py. window is the number of tokens on each side of an anchor term.

adjective_anchor_terms._comment: Used by adjective_window.py. Each key is an anchor concept; its list is that concept's surface forms in primary_language.

dependency_parsing._comment: Used by dependency_parsing.py. chunk_chars is how much text is fed to spaCy at once.

dependency_agents._comment: Used by dependency_parsing.py. role is a dependency label (e.g. 'nsubj', 'obj'); passive and English-convention spellings (nsubjpass, nsubj:pass, dobj) are matched automatically.

cross_corpus_concept_clusters._comment: Used by cross_corpus_frequency.py. Each cluster has one key per language code (must match your languages' codes) holding that language's surface/inflected forms for the same concept.

cross_corpus_dependency._comment: Used by cross_corpus_dependency.py. agent_a/agent_b are arbitrary role names — see README. 'primary' is spaCy-side (lemmas, primary_language); 'comparison' is Stanza-side (surface forms, comparison_language).

topic_modeling._comment: Used by analysis_b_topics.py. min_topic_size is the smallest number of chunks BERTopic will call a topic — lower it for small corpora. The remaining keys are language codes; extra_stopwords supplements load_stopwords(), keep_stopwords exempts specific words from removal.
